stem.text: Find the first three terms in the Maclaurin's series for sinh–1(x + 1) in the form lna + bx + cx2, giving the exact values of the constants a, b and c.

points.text: f′(x) = (1 + (x + 1)2)–1/2; finds first derivative. Accept 1/(x+1+√((x+1)2+1)) · (1 + (2x+2)/(2√((x+1)2+1))) or implicit y′coshy=1
f″(x) = –(1 + (x + 1)2)–3/2(x + 1); finds second derivative. Allow not simplified or implicit y″coshy+(y′)2sinhy=0
f′(0) = 1/√2, f″(0) = –1/(2√2); evaluates their derivatives at zero only — must have attempted both derivatives

explanation.text: sinh<sup>–1</sup>(x + 1) is not one of the standard listed Maclaurin series, so the expansion has to be built directly: find f(x) = sinh<sup>–1</sup>(x + 1), differentiate twice, evaluate f(0), f′(0) and f″(0), then substitute into f(x) ≈ f(0) + f′(0)x + f″(0)x²/2!.

The derivative of sinh<sup>–1</sup>u is 1/√(1 + u²); with u = x + 1 and the chain rule, f′(x) = (1 + (x+1)²)^(–1/2). Differentiating again (chain rule on the power, then product rule for the extra (x+1) factor) gives f″(x) = –(1 + (x+1)²)^(–3/2)(x+1).

reasoningChain: Differentiate f(x) = sinh⁻¹(x + 1) using d/du[sinh⁻¹u] = 1/√(1+u²) and the chain rule to get f′(x).
Differentiate f′(x) again (chain rule + product rule) to get f″(x).
Evaluate f(0) = sinh⁻¹1 = ln(1 + √2) using the standard log form of sinh⁻¹.
Evaluate f′(0) = 1/√2 and f″(0) = –1/(2√2) by substituting x = 0 into both derivatives.
Substitute into the Maclaurin form f(0) + f′(0)x + f″(0)x²/2! and simplify the x² coefficient (dividing f″(0) by 2!).

inferredMistakes.text: Forgetting to divide f″(0) by 2! before writing the x² coefficient, giving c = –1/(2√2) instead of the correct –1/(4√2).
Missing the chain-rule factor from differentiating the inner (x + 1), since d/dx[(x+1)] = 1 makes the omission easy to overlook but it still affects the (x+1) coefficient inside f″(x).
